title: Alakh Pandey Physics Wallah Leadership: Improve Student Experience | Ashish Kumar Chaudhary posted on the topic | LinkedIn
text:
Alakh Pandey Physics Wallah (PW) Gopal Sharma Prateek Maheshwari#PhysicsWallah#StudentFirst#ParentVoice#Education#EdTech#CustomerExperience#Leadership#QualityEducation#ContinuousImprovement An Open Appeal to Physics Wallah Leadership: Does "Empowering 25 Crore Youth of Bharat" End at Enrollment? Dear Mr. Alakh Pandey and the Physics Wallah Leadership Team, This is not a campaign against Physics Wallah. I appreciate the tremendous contribution Physics Wallah has made in making quality education affordable and accessible to millions of students. I also deeply respect the teachers whose dedication has transformed countless young lives. However, as a parent and a professional with over 25 years of leadership experience, I believe every great organization grows by listening to genuine customer feedback. I enrolled my child in the Physics Wallah Power Batch, trusting your vision of "Mission to Empower 25 Crore Youth of Bharat by 2030." Our family invested approximately ₹42,000 in this 9-month program, and every installment was paid on time. Unfortunately, our experience after enrollment has raised serious concerns. Our experience: Dedicated Mentor: Despite being a key feature of the Power Batch, there was little proactive mentoring, academic guidance, or follow-up on my child's progress. Communication Gap: My child missed an important examination due to the absence of timely notifications or reminders. Even after repeated escalations, no satisfactory explanation or preventive action was provided. Delayed Study Material: Although enrollment was completed in May 2026, the promised study material was significantly delayed despite multiple follow-ups. Access Blocked Despite Timely Payment: The app showed 15 July 2026 as the installment due date. I paid on the due date, yet my child's access to the live class was blocked, resulting in the loss of an important session. While access was later restored with an apology, the missed learning opportunity could not be recovered. My concern is not about the teachers—it is about the systems and operational processes that support students after enrollment. I respectfully request Physics Wallah to strengthen: Automated reminders for exams and important deadlines. Real-time payment updates to prevent unnecessary access blocks. Clearly defined mentor accountability. Timely dispatch of study materials with measurable service standards. A faster and more transparent grievance resolution process. Mr. Alakh Pandey, your vision has inspired millions of parents, including me. My humble request is that the student experience after enrollment reflects the same commitment as the mission itself. In education, trust is not built by marketing alone—it is earned through consistent delivery, accountability, and genuine student care. I sincerely hope this feedback is received in the spirit in which it is intended: constructive, respectful, and focused on improving the experience of every student.

Edtech company Physicswallah Ltd on Thursday (July 16) said its board has approved the acquisition of an additional 11% stake in Guiding Light Education Technologies Private Ltd (Sarrthi IAS) for a total consideration of ₹71.81 crore. The acquisition will involve the purchase of 1,100 equity shares of Sarrthi IAS. Following the completion of the Tranche II acquisition, Physicswallah’s shareholding in Sarrthi IAS will increase from 40% to 51%, after which Sarrthi IAS will become a subsidiary of the company. Physicswallah had entered into a Shareholders’ Agreement and Share Purchase Agreement with Sarrthi IAS and its promoters on September 2, 2025, for acquiring up to 85% of the fully diluted equity share capital of the company in six tranches during financial years 2026 to 2031. The company has already completed Tranche I of the transaction and currently holds a 40% stake in Sarrthi IAS, making it an associate company. The board has approved an addendum to the Share Purchase Agreement to record mutually agreed revisions related to the valuation methodology and purchase consideration applicable to Tranche II. Other terms of the transaction documents, including acquisition of remaining tranches through the prescribed EBITDA-based valuation mechanism, will remain unchanged. Sarrthi IAS operates in the education sector and provides online and offline coaching and test preparation services for civil services and other competitive examinations. According to the company, Sarrthi IAS had a turnover of ₹76.52 crore in financial year 2025-26, compared with ₹28.46 crore in FY2024-25 and ₹1.04 crore in FY2023-24. The target company had a paid-up share capital of ₹1 lakh and net worth of ₹33.96 crore. The transaction does not fall under related party transactions, and the acquisition is being undertaken at arm’s length based on an independent valuation report. Physicswallah said the acquisition is aimed at strengthening its presence in the UPSC and civil services examination preparation segment. PhysicsWallah recently increased its stake in Sarrthi IAS from 40% to 51%, making it a subsidiary.

PhysicsWallah wasn't entering the UPSC market.

...
So instead of replacing PW OnlyIAS...PhysicsWallah now has two brands serving the same market.

That is why I don't think this acquisition is about launching UPSC.

It is about strengthening PhysicsWallah's position within the UPSC ecosystem.

> Curious to hear how others think about this.

text: Physics Wallah (PW) founder Alakh Pandey has announced a new initiative aimed at supporting aspiring entrepreneurs who have promising startup ideas but lack the financial resources to bring them to life. In a video message shared on social media, Pandey encouraged students and young innovators to reach out if they have a strong business idea but are unable to pursue it due to a lack of funding. Emphasizing that his motivation is to contribute to the country's growth, he said, "Take money from me and do something for India and for yourself. In return, I don't want anything." As part of the initiative, Pandey shared a dedicated contact number through which aspiring founders can submit their startup ideas. He said he will personally review submissions and try to support deserving entrepreneurs, giving them an opportunity to transform their ideas into real businesses. The announcement has received widespread attention across India's startup ecosystem, where access to early-stage capital remains one of the biggest challenges for first-time founders. Beyond financial assistance, many young entrepreneurs also struggle to find mentorship, guidance, and the confidence needed to launch their ventures. Pandey's initiative reflects the evolving role of Physics Wallah, which has grown from an online education platform into one of India's most trusted brands among students. By encouraging entrepreneurship alongside education, the initiative aims to inspire more young Indians to become job creators rather than job seekers.#alakhpandey#physicswallah#pw#startup#startupindia#entrepreneurship#founders#innovation#funding#students#youngfounders#businessnews#india#edtech
